# BLO-37868 — bound SAFE_LITERAL env values at the shared choke point

Files:

- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

Every literal `NAME=value` environment string is subject to Linux's
`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` limit, not only the prompt and wake-payload variables fixed
by [BLO-36854](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-36854) and
[BLO-37287](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-37287). The workspace
and runtime-service JSON arrays were unbounded and could kill the pod with
`E2BIG` before the model turn.

The adapter now bounds `SAFE_LITERAL` values in `buildEnvVars`: JSON arrays are
reduced to the longest fitting prefix (or `[]` when that fits), oversized names
are dropped when no value can fit, and `PAPERCLIP_ENV_SHED_JSON` records the
original byte counts. The marker is emitted only when shedding occurs and
contains names and integers, so reduction is visible without copying shed
contents into another env value. Sensitive `secretKeyRef` values are left
unchanged because silently dropping credentials would be worse than the
startup failure.

Tests drive an oversized array through every non-prefix `SAFE_LITERAL`, assert
the all-container kernel-size invariant, preserve useful array prefixes,
cover marker presence/absence and the oversized-name boundary, and mutation-
check the `[]` budget fallback.
